input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='index.html'; s=open(p).read()
a='''          cell.setAttribute("data-piece", ch === type ? type : "");\n'''
assert s.count(a)==1; s=s.replace(a,''); open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
sed -n '/<script>/,/<\/script>/p' index.html | sed '1d;$d' > "$TMPDIR/t.js" 2>/dev/null || true
node --check "$TMPDIR/t.js" && echo ok; grep -n '"over"' index.html

content.text:
I added the three-piece preview and the game-over state to `index.html`. I haven't run it in a browser; I only checked that the script parses.
- **Preview:** it always shows three pieces, soonest first. The queue now refills after every spawn and after `setQueue`, so a fixed queue keeps its order with random pieces added after it. Each piece has `data-testid="next-piece-item"` and `data-piece`, and uses its board colour. I took `data-piece` off the small cells inside, so it only appears on the items.
- **Game over:** a spawn that doesn't fit sets status to `"gameover"` (it was `"over"`) and shows the overlay, now tagged `data-testid="game-over"`. Gravity steps and player actions already did nothing unless the game is running; Enter still starts a new game.
